_doc: WS5 coverage matrix — one entry per county recorder. access: scrape | bulk-export | operator-export | manual-request | unavailable | unverified. Only counties with verified=true had their access level confirmed (date + method recorded); 'unverified' entries carry the best-known lead and MUST be checked in a browser before relying on them (several portals block automated verification via robots.txt — respected, not bypassed).
law_note: Mining claims become public record at the county recorder FIRST: location notices are recorded under state law (Idaho Code tit. 47, ch. 15), and the federal FLPMA filing with BLM is due within 90 days of location (43 U.S.C. § 1744). BLM adjudication + MLRS indexing add more lag, so the county index can lead MLRS by weeks to months — that gap is the WS5 signal.
doc_types: AFFIDAVIT OF ASSESSMENT WORK / PROOF OF LABOR / INTENT TO HOLD

cassia.verify_method: cassia.gov/recorder fetched: no online index or vendor portal listed; public computer + records vault by appointment (call/email ahead); Public Records Request form (fillable PDF) to recorder@cassia.gov
cassia.notes: Copies ~$1/page. Pre-1976 location notices live in physical grantor/grantee books (no digital index). Ask specifically for the mining index if one exists — many Idaho recorders keep a separate mining-locations index book.

twin_falls.notes: No vendor confirmed from sandbox. Check the recorder page in a browser; third-party indexes (deeds.com, NETR) list the office but not a public search portal.

minidoka.notes: County site has a 'Recorded Land Records' page (minidoka.id.us/448) that reportedly points to iDoc Market (idocmarket.com — subscription; index search typically free after signup). Site blocked automated verification (robots.txt/timeout) — confirm in a browser. If confirmed: access becomes operator-export (search the index in the browser, export/copy results to data-inbox/county/minidoka/).

power.notes: Small county; likely manual-request. Not probed.

box_elder.notes: Adjacent to Cassia across the UT line (Black Pine / Raft River trend continues south). Confirm portal in a browser.

elko.notes: Elko County has historically run a self-hosted recorded-document search — worth a browser check; NV recorders commonly index mining locations well (huge claim volume).
